value: This article elaborates on "Computational Trinitarianism," a foundational insight asserting a profound equivalence between formal logic (specifically type theory), programming languages (computation), and higher category theory. This perspective posits that these seemingly disparate fields are merely different manifestations of a singular underlying notion of computation, with key correspondences including "propositions as types," "proofs as programs," and the deep relationship between type theory and category theory. The discussion extends to "tetralogies" that incorporate algebraic topology/cohomology for both classical and quantum computation, providing a "Rosetta Stone" mapping of concepts to highlight their unified structure across these domains.
